summary: Okta token-size enforcement causing 400s on Feature Flags admin console login
description:
Issue summary:
Users are receiving HTTP 400 / 'invalid_request: token_too_large' responses when attempting to sign in to the internal Feature Flags admin console. The problem began after an Okta configuration rollout that enabled stricter token size enforcement on SAML/OIDC assertions.

Impact:
- Engineers cannot access Feature Flags admin UI to modify rollout rules and emergency feature toggles.
- On-call workflows (hotfix rollouts) are blocked for any team that relies on the console.
- Incident response window lengthened due to inability to temporarily flip flags.

Environment:
- Affected app: feature-flags-admin (internal console)
- Environment: prod-us-east (internal tooling network)
- Identity provider: Okta (org-wide policy change rolled out 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Navigate to https://internal.featureflags.redwood/ and click 'Sign in with Okta'.
2) Authenticate through Okta SSO flow for a user with > 20 group memberships (common for platform/admins).
3) Okta redirects back to identity-proxy with SAML/OIDC token; the proxy returns 400 and the browser shows 'invalid_request: token_too_large'.

Observed behavior:
- Immediate 400 response from identity-proxy with message referencing token size limits.
- No user session is created; UI shows login error.
- Okta admin audit logs show policy enforcement events coincident with the timing of failed logins.

Expected behavior:
- Successful SSO exchange and creation of an internal session for the console.

Initial hypothesis:
- Okta recently enabled a new token-size enforcement rule for assertion length (related to group claim expansion). Users with many group memberships produce tokens that exceed the new limit; identity-proxy rejects long tokens leading to 400s.

Relevant links/runbooks/logs:
- Slack: #support (thread t/okta-token-size-2026-03-12)
- Okta admin audit: https://okta.redwood/admin/audit?event=token_enforcement (internal)
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/runbooks/identity-proxy-token-failures (internal)

Temporary mitigation attempted so far:
- Reproduced with a test account and confirmed group-count correlates with failure.
- Support temporarily re-routed a small subset of requests to fallback-idp (unavailable for most internal apps) — partial mitigation for one team.
- Okta admin contacted to confirm the policy change and request a rollback or scoped exception for internal tooling while we implement a fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Click 'Sign in with Okta' on Feature Flags admin UI. 2) Complete Okta login for a user with >15 group memberships. 3) Observe 400 response from identity-proxy: 'invalid_request: token_too_large' and no session creation.

investigation_notes:
- Confirmed timing matches Okta org policy rollout (2026-03-12 04:00 UTC).
- Token length correlates with number of group memberships; test accounts with <10 groups succeed.
- identity-proxy has an internal maximum accepted token size of ~12KB in middleware (limitation introduced by the SAML parsing library upgrade in 2026-02).
- Options considered: 1) Ask Okta to rollback/scoped-exception, 2) Increase identity-proxy token size ceiling, 3) Trim group claims (claim reduction) at Okta or proxy.
- Risk assessment: Increasing proxy token size requires a careful memory/DoS review; claim-trimming on Okta requires policy changes and may affect RBAC resolution for other apps.
- Reproduced locally with an assertion fixture; created a test PR to add logging and guardrails to identity-proxy parsing (github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1423).
comments: 2026-03-12 05:02 - Sofia Mendes (SRE): Initial triage complete. Confirmed 400 originates from identity-proxy middleware. Reproduced with test token. Linking to INT-224466 for token parsing change history.

2026-03-12 06:20 - Priya Sharma (IAM): Okta tenant team says policy was enabled org-wide to mitigate oversized assertion attacks. They're open to a scoped exception for the feature-flags app while we remediate.

2026-03-12 07:15 - Liam O'Connor (assignee): Implementing short-term proxy-side increase to token size ceiling on a canary in staging to validate memory characteristics (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/identity-proxy/pull/1423). Will monitor for increased CPU/memory on canary node.
2026-03-12 09:40 - Aisha Patel (reporter): Several oncall shifts affected; please prioritize exception if available — safety-critical toggles blocked for infra team.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Okta Admin Team: Scoped exception created for app-client-id ff-admin-client (valid for 72 hours). Please proceed with code changes and schedule permanent fix.
2026-03-13 02:30 - Liam O'Connor: Staging canary shows no memory spike with increased limit to 32KB. Preparing rollout plan for prod canary at 03:30 UTC with automated rollback on OOM or error surge.
resolution: Triage complete. Okta granted a 72-hour scoped exception for ff-admin-client to restore access. Staged an identity-proxy code change to increase token ceiling to 32KB with monitoring and memory guards. Next steps: prod canary rollout, formalizing claim-trimming plan with IAM, and add long-term mitigation to identity runbook.
next_steps: Prod canary rollout of identity-proxy token ceiling change (03:30 UTC 2026-03-13)
Add claim-trimming policy to Okta for internal apps and plan for phased rollouts
Finalize PR review and post-deploy monitoring dashboard for token-size metrics
slo_impact: Feature Flags admin console unavailable for some users for ~5 hours during initial detection; scoped exception restored most users. No customer-facing SLOs impacted (internal-only tool).
